sections.h2: Who to call about a Harnett County tax bill
sections.html:
The Harnett County Tax Department, based in Lillington, lists, appraises and bills every parcel in the county, and its Collection Division takes the payments. For a value, call the Real Property Division at 910-814-6920. For a bill or a payment, call 910-893-7520 or write to taxinfo@harnett.org.

Collections are at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Suite 101, Lillington, NC 27546. The register of deeds uses the same street address at Suite 200, which is handy when a sale needs both a payoff figure and a recorded deed.

Real property is listed automatically every year, so owners do not receive an annual listing form. Owners are asked to report new structures and additions, and county appraisers work from building permits issued by the county or a municipal permit office.

The Harnett payment clock starts September 1 and stays penalty-free through January 5. On January 6 the balance picks up 2%, then 3/4% for every further month, as in G.S. 105-360.

For the 2026 bills, January 5, 2027 is the final day before delinquency. Owners can pay in equal monthly amounts or in any amount they choose while the bill is open, and each payment is applied to the bill with an updated statement mailed back.

Bills can be settled through the online portal, the phone line at 1-866-580-9996, the mail, or the counter, and only the counter takes cash. Checks, certified checks and money orders work at the counter or through the mail.

  • Personal debit cards carry a $3.80 convenience fee per transaction.
  • Credit cards are charged 2.50% of the balance.
  • Business credit or debit cards on high-rewards programs carry 3.25%.
  • E-checks carry $2.00 per transaction.

The processor keeps those fees. A bounced check voids the payment, and the bill is charged the larger of 10% of the check or $25.00. The office makes no payment arrangements once a bill is delinquent, so installment payers should begin before January 6.

sections.h2: How Harnett County values a house
sections.html:
The Real Property Division sets fair market value for the county's 73,000-plus parcels with a CAMA system. Inputs include site visits, zoning and soil classes, deeds, market sales and aerial photos.

The reappraisal of January 1, 2022 was followed by a move to a four-year cycle on the revenue department's recommendation, which put the next reappraisal at January 1, 2026. State law sets the outer limit at eight years under G.S. 105-286.

A structure is valued by its percent complete on January 1. A garage finished in March adds nothing to that year's bill. If you have just built or renovated, the value on the bill may lag the real condition of the house.

Start by asking the Real Property Division how it handles value reviews after the 2026 reappraisal, and go to the county's review board if that conversation leaves a gap. Commissioners usually sit as that board, and G.S. 105-322 sets its opening session between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May.

  • Request a hearing, by letter or by appearing, before the board adjourns.
  • A written decision follows within a month of adjournment.
  • A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission, with notice due thirty days after that decision is mailed.

Bring comparable sales close to the house, contractor estimates and dated photos. A value tied to January 1 of the reappraisal year is easier to contest with evidence from that date.

Harnett County also offers an exemptions page and a present-use value program for farm and forest land. Three state programs for a permanent residence run through the assessor on Form AV-9, and an owner may draw on just one of them.

  • An elderly or disabled owner can exclude the larger of $25,000 or half the assessed worth of the home, if 2025 income stayed under $38,800.
  • A disabled veteran's home gets a flat $45,000 cut in taxable value, with no age or income test.
  • The circuit breaker holds tax to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% for incomes between $38,800 and $58,200, and defers the remainder as a lien.

File during the January listing period; late forms are still taken until June 1. The deferral ends at transfer, and the deferred taxes for the three prior fiscal years are then payable, so a seller using it should expect that balance at closing.

sections.h2: What follows when a bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Liens on unpaid real estate tax are advertised each spring in The Daily Record, under the name of the owner on January 6, with an advertising fee added to the bill.

Harnett mostly uses the mortgage-style foreclosure method, a civil action ending in a courthouse-steps auction by a court-appointed commissioner. The sale calls for a 10% deposit, then a 10-day upset bid window, and each upset bid must top the last by 5% or $750, whichever is greater. The owner can redeem before confirmation by paying all taxes, fees and costs.

The state issues no tax lien certificates, so an outsider who pays someone else's delinquent bill gets no title. Foreclosure usually comes after the office has tried bank attachments, wage garnishment, rent attachment and a sheriff's levy.

Whoever owns the parcel at closing settles its tax, and the payoff is taken out of sale money at the closing table. Get a written balance from the Collection Division, with interest and any advertising fee included, before closing is scheduled.

The register of deeds collects a separate deed tax before recording, and the seller carries it. A house with delinquent tax, a foreclosure filing or a deferred balance can still sell, provided the lender and tax office are paid in the right order. A cash buyer will want the same clear title, so the payoff works the same way.

Harnett County has about 150,137 residents, up 12.4% from the 2020 base, and 59,085 housing units, 71.0% of them owner-occupied. The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $246,200, and median household income is $71,287. Permits issued during 2025 numbered 2,205. These figures help set expectations for pricing and timing.

faqs.q: Does Harnett County reward early payment?
faqs.a: No. The county offers no discount on ad valorem property tax. Owners can make prepayments from February through August, which spreads the cost but earns no reduction.

faqs.q: What is the final day to pay a Harnett bill without a penalty?
faqs.a: January 5, following the September 1 due date. For the 2026 bills that is January 5, 2027, and interest begins the next morning.

faqs.q: Is a sale possible while Harnett taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. The title agent remits the tax, interest and any advertising fee out of the seller's funds, so request an up-to-date payoff figure from the Collection Division first. A filed foreclosure case adds court costs and attorney fees to that figure.

faqs.q: Does Harnett County reappraise property every year?
faqs.a: No. The county moved to a four-year cycle after its January 1, 2022 reappraisal. Between reappraisals, values change when a property changes, such as new construction or an addition.

faqs.q: Where do I pay or ask about a Harnett County tax bill?
faqs.a: Use the online portal, the phone line at 1-866-580-9996, the mail, or the counter at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Suite 101, Lillington. Questions about a bill go to 910-893-7520 or taxinfo@harnett.org.
